source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Lead-pipe rigidity and reduced reflexes developing gradually after exposure to a dopamine-blocking drug.","B":"Hyperreflexia and clonus developing rapidly after a serotonergic medication is started or increased.","C":"Flaccid weakness with absent clonus and no increase in reflexes after a medication change.","D":"Fever without clonus, hyperreflexia, rigidity, or another characteristic neuromuscular finding."}}
source_row.rationale: Serotonin syndrome is distinguished by neuromuscular hyperreactivity, especially clonus and hyperreflexia, and often develops quickly after serotonergic exposure or a medication change. Option B is correct. Lead-pipe rigidity and slower evolution are more typical of NMS, while C and D lack the characteristic serotonin-syndrome neuromuscular findings.
source_row.source_detail: Differential diagnosis/clinical features: serotonin syndrome develops rapidly after serotonergic exposure/change and is characterized by neuromuscular hyperreactivity, especially hyperreflexia and clonus; NMS more often has marked rigidity and a slower onset. StatPearls Serotonin Syndrome updated 2024-03-02 and current in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
